title: Short-Form Video Editor
description: Short-Form Video Editor (Premiere Pro + After Effects, or DaVinci Resolve), Full-Time Remote, UK Agency About Us We're a London-based creative content consultancy producing short-form social content for a small portfolio of growing brands. Tight team, fast pace, no bureaucracy. Strict NDA on client names. The Role You'll edit 10 to 20 short-form pieces per week in Premiere Pro with After Effects, or DaVinci Resolve with Fusion — your call, work in whichever you ship fastest in. Footage and assets are delivered to you via Frame.io and Google Drive. You cut, caption, motion-design, sound-design, colour, and export to spec. We review, you revise, we ship. What you'll be editing (three repeating formats) 1) Podcast clips, talking-head with motion design 60 to 90 second vertical cuts pulled from long-form podcast recordings. Two-camera setup, separate audio tracks. Punchy hooks in the first 3 seconds, animated captions on-brand, lower thirds, light motion graphics (kinetic type, callouts, simple transitions). Sometimes paired with a matching square carousel for LinkedIn (5 to 8 slides in After Effects or Resolve Fusion, exported as PNGs or 1x1 video). 2) Talking-head videos with supplied B-roll 30 to 90 second vertical or square edits where we send you the A-roll (presenter to camera) and a B-roll package. You cut the talking head tightly, motivate B-roll insertions, add captions, light sound design, colour-match A and B-roll. No need to source footage — it's all supplied. 3) Static and animated carousels (occasional) LinkedIn and Instagram square carousels built from supplied copy and brand templates. 5 to 10 slides. Sometimes a short animated version for the lead slide. Weekly deliverables - 10 to 20 short-form pieces, mostly 15 to 90 seconds - Burned-in captions, brand-styled per client, accurate to audio - B-roll cutaways motivated by content (not pasted on top) - Light motion design (kinetic captions, callouts, lower thirds, end cards) - Clean H.264 exports to platform spec (1080x1920, 1080x1080, 1920x1080) - Organised project files returned to shared drive Must have - Fluent in either Premiere Pro + After Effects OR DaVinci Resolve + Fusion - Strong captioning craft (kinetic, on-brand, accurate, not auto-generated garbage) - Portfolio of at least 5 short-form edits you personally cut, including at least one podcast clip and one talking-head with B-roll - Fluent written and conversational English - Wired internet, minimum 50 Mbps down / 20 up - Machine able to run your chosen software smoothly, minimum 16GB RAM, dedicated GPU - Daily 4-hour overlap with UK hours (3pm to 11pm Manila works) Nice to have - Real motion design chops (kinetic type, simple 2D animation in AE or Fusion) - Carousel and static design (Photoshop, Illustrator, or Figma) - Sound design and audio cleanup (iZotope RX, Fairlight, Audition) - Real colour grading beyond auto-balance - Familiarity with Frame.io, Notion, Slack Pay £500/month flat (approx PHP 35,000), paid via Wise on the 1st. 60-day review for raise to £550 to £650 based on quality and ownership. Paid trial task before hire: $40 USD flat on delivery. 13th-month bonus paid in December as standard. Mon to Fri, 6 to 8 hours daily. Your weekends are yours. How to apply 1. Start your email with the word "PARSNIP" as the first line. 2. Send to ---------- a) A 60-second Loom introducing yourself, showing your editing machine, and explaining one decision you made on a recent edit and why. b) Links to 3 short-form edits you personally cut. At least one podcast clip and one talking-head with B-roll. Tell me which one you're most proud of and which one you'd redo. c) Screenshot of fast.com speed test and your software version numbers. d) Your monthly rate expectation. e) One sentence: "What's the most common mistake editors make on the first 3 seconds of a short-form video?" 3. Subject line: PARSNIP, Short-Form Editor, [Your Name] We respond within 5 working days to every application.

title: Senior-Level Graphic Designer
description: We Are Hiring: Senior-Level Graphic Designer We are on the lookout for a highly skilled and experienced senior-level graphic designer to join our team on a long-term, ongoing, month-to-month basis. This is a role for a seasoned professional who can bring technical expertise, creative problem-solving, and a meticulous eye for detail to every project. What We’re Looking For We need a designer who: - Has strong technical design skills and a keen eye for detail. - Can self-manage projects and timelines to ensure on-time delivery without constant oversight. - Excels at following directions and adhering to project guidelines. Required Skills To excel in this role, you must have: - Expert-level proficiency in Adobe Creative Suite (InDesign, Illustrator, and Photoshop). - Prepress knowledge and experience, including converting colors for print and file packaging. - The ability to correct minor errors, such as inconsistent capitalization in client-delivered content. - Exceptional attention to detail and the ability to follow directions precisely. - A creative approach to problem-solving. - Strong typography skills (e.g., fixing rags and kerning appropriately). - Real-world client experience. - The ability to recognize your limits and know when to push them. Bonus Skills If you have any of the following, you’ll stand out even more: - WordPress expertise (especially with DIVI). - Content writing capabilities. - Illustration skills. Typical Projects Here’s a glimpse of the types of projects you’ll work on: - Creating website mockups in Photoshop. - Laying out print brochures. - Updating or designing print ads. - Developing brand designs. - Crafting multipage brochures for companies. How We Work - We use Trello to manage projects. - Projects are typically assigned during the first half of the week. - Questions about a project should be asked within a day or two of assignment. - Working files must always be stored on our cloud drive. - Project time is tracked using our time-tracking software. - You’ll be provided with brand assets, working files, and access to stock images and graphics as needed. Compensation - This position pays $15 USD per hour. --- How to Apply To be considered, you must follow these instructions carefully. Applications that do not meet these requirements will not be reviewed. Please provide: 1. A portfolio with at least 10 work samples. (If you only send 10 samples, prioritize longer-form design content such as reports, full ad campaigns, and white papers. Limit logos/brand designs to no more than two, and no more than two should be social media-related.) 2. Your Resume/CV. 3. A written explanation of what uniquely qualifies you for this position. 4. A response to the following: Are there any skills listed under “Required Skills” that you do not have? If so, explain why you feel you should still be considered. 5. A response to the following: Do you have any of the “Bonus Skills”? If yes, explain. If you have additional skills, let us know! 6. Confirmation of whether you consider yourself detail-oriented and able to follow directions precisely. 7. Your availability for a video interview in the next week (include days and times in EST). 8. Your availability to work (hours per week).

title: AutoCAD Drafter— Traffic Control Plans
description: We're commissioning a series of traffic control plans (work zone / road-work TCPs) based on existing reference standards. We need an experienced CAD drafter for an ongoing project, starting with a small paid trial. What this involves: - Working from a set of standard reference drawings that we'll provide. - For each one, producing matched sets — a reference version that follows the source standard exactly, plus several variations of it that deliberately deviate from the standard in specific, controlled ways. - Each plan must be produced in AutoCAD at actual scale, with the DXF model space in feet. The geometry must match the labels: if a distance is labeled "320 ft," the measured distance between the relevant sign insertion points in the DXF must equal 320 ft. This is the most important requirement of the project — many drafters label distances without actually drawing them to scale, and that won't work here. - For each plan, also producing a sidecar annotation file (JSON) recording the key dimensions used and, for the deviating versions, what was changed and where (with DXF coordinates). - Final output per plan: a layered DXF file in feet, plus the matching JSON file. Trial: We start with a small paid batch (6 plans from a single source). If the work is good, we scale up significantly from there — hundreds of plans over the following months. Pricing structure: - The 6-plan trial: paid at an agreed rate. - After the trial, the next ~10–15 plans are paid hourly while you build templates and internalize the workflow. - Once you're producing plans steadily, we switch to a per-plan rate based on your actual time during the hourly phase. The per-plan rate is structured so your effective hourly earnings stay higher than during ramp-up — efficient work pays off. Requirements: - Strong AutoCAD proficiency. Comfortable working in DXF/DWG with model-space units in feet, and you understand block insertion points. - Ability to read technical standards and apply them precisely — looking up values in tables, following the right formulas for the right cases. - Attention to detail. Geometry must match labels exactly. We will verify by measuring the DXF. - Comfortable producing structured JSON files alongside CAD output. - Good English communication. Helpful but not required: - Prior experience with traffic control plans, work zone drawings, or U.S.-style roadway standards. How to apply: 1. Sometimes you will receive a full Figma design to build from. Other times you will design the pages yourself in Figma based on a brief, get approval, and then build. You need to be comfortable with both workflows. Our copywriter handles all website content. Your job is to make that content look great on the page — the visual hierarchy, the layout, the spacing, the typography, the overall feel. Copy will either be placed directly into Figma designs for you or provided separately for you to integrate during the build. Here is what the day-to-day looks like: Design - Design website pages and layouts in Figma based on provided briefs, page structures, and brand guidelines - Create clean, modern designs with strong visual hierarchy — a visitor should know exactly where to look and what to do on every page - Maintain consistent spacing, typography, colour usage, and component patterns across every page of a site - Design with conversion in mind — the layout should guide the visitor toward the CTA, not just look pretty - Design responsive layouts — you think about how the page works on tablet and mobile during the design phase, not as an afterthought - Apply brand guidelines accurately — colours, fonts, logo usage, imagery style - Design reusable components and sections that can be used across multiple pages and client sites - Present design work for review and iterate based on feedback quickly Build - Build approved designs in WordPress using Bricks Builder — the live site must match the Figma design accurately - Implement responsive behaviour across desktop, tablet, and mobile — every breakpoint should look intentional and polished - Keep builds clean, lightweight, and well-structured — no bloated code, no unnecessary plugins, no messy class naming - Optimise for page speed — image compression, lazy loading, minimal CSS/JS, clean markup. Sites need to score well on PageSpeed Insights. - Implement on-page SEO fundamentals as directed — heading hierarchy (H1, H2, H3), image alt text, clean URL structures, schema-ready markup - Set up and configure essential plugins — forms, analytics, caching, security, SEO (Yoast or RankMath) - Build reusable templates and global elements in Bricks — headers, footers, section templates that can be maintained centrally - Test thoroughly before handover — cross-browser testing, mobile testing, form testing, link checking, speed testing - Troubleshoot and fix issues — if something breaks or does not look right, you own it and fix it without being chased General - Manage multiple client website projects at the same time without dropping quality or missing deadlines - Communicate clearly on progress, blockers, and timelines — you flag issues early, not after a deadline passes - Follow SOPs and checklists for design and build processes - Stay current with Bricks Builder updates, WordPress best practices, and modern web design trends --- MUST-HAVE EXPERIENCE (NON-NEGOTIABLE) - Proven experience designing websites in Figma — not just wireframes or mockups. Full page designs with proper typography, spacing, visual hierarchy, and responsive considerations. You must have a portfolio showing this. - Strong WordPress build experience using Bricks Builder specifically — you know how to use Bricks to build custom layouts, work with conditions, create templates, and structure sites properly. If your only experience is Elementor or Divi, this is not the right role. - Ability to translate a Figma design to a live WordPress site accurately — what you design is what you build. No "close enough." Pixel-level attention to detail. - Strong responsive design skills — you build for desktop, tablet, and mobile deliberately. Not just letting things stack and hoping it looks fine. - Understanding of page speed optimisation — you know how to keep a WordPress site fast. Image optimisation, minimal plugin usage, clean code, caching basics. - Understanding of basic on-page SEO implementation — heading hierarchy, image alt text, clean URLs, meta fields. You do not need to be an SEO specialist but you need to implement the fundamentals correctly. - Understanding of basic CRO and UX principles — you design and build pages that guide visitors toward an action. You think about visual hierarchy, whitespace, CTA placement, and user flow. - Experience designing and building websites for service-based or lead-generation businesses — not just ecommerce, not just personal blogs. - Ability to work from briefs and direction — you receive a brief, brand guidelines, and copy, and you produce a polished result. You do not need to be told every detail but you follow the structure and direction given. - Ability to manage multiple projects at once without dropping quality or missing timelines. - Self-motivation and accountability — you do not wait to be chased. You flag issues, meet deadlines, and take ownership of your work. If your experience is only Elementor or Divi — do not apply. If you only design but do not build — do not apply. If you only build but cannot design in Figma — do not apply. If your portfolio is only personal projects or template customisations — do not apply. --- NICE TO HAVE - Experience with other WordPress builders (Zion Builder, Oxygen, Breakdance) in addition to Bricks - Experience with WooCommerce or membership site builds - Basic PHP, CSS, or JavaScript knowledge for custom tweaks beyond what Bricks provides out of the box - Experience with GoHighLevel landing page builds or embeds - Experience working with a copywriter or content team — receiving copy and integrating it into designs rather than writing it yourself - Familiarity with Google Tag Manager, conversion tracking setup, or analytics implementation - Experience creating Loom walkthroughs of your design or build process - Animation and interaction design experience — tasteful micro-interactions, scroll-triggered animations, hover states - Experience with website accessibility basics (WCAG) --- THIS ROLE IS NOT A FIT IF - You only use Elementor or Divi - You only design or only build — not both - You rely on pre-made templates and just swap content - Your builds are slow, bloated, or plugin-heavy - You are not comfortable working in Figma - You cannot build responsive sites that look good on every device - You prefer heavy strategy or client-facing project management — this is a design and build role, not a strategist role - You are uncomfortable working from briefs and direction - You need to be chased for updates or deadlines THIS ROLE IS A FIT IF - You are strong in Figma and confident designing full website pages from a brief - You can build exactly what you design in Bricks Builder - You care about clean execution — pixel-level accuracy, fast load times, responsive on every device - You work well from clear instructions and structures - You can manage multiple builds at once without things falling apart - You want to focus on design and build, not strategy or project management - You take pride in your work and own the quality of every site you deliver --- WHY WORK WITH US - Work directly with the founder — no middle management - No micromanagement — clear briefs, clear ownership, clear accountability - You will have a dedicated copywriter providing all website content — you focus on design and build, not writing - Long-term clients across multiple industries — stable, varied workload - Fast-moving agency that values speed and quality equally - No-fluff, performance-focused environment - Remote role with consistent hours and weekly pay --- HOURS AND PAY - Remote role (Philippines preferred) - Working hours: 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM AWST - Weekly pay via Wise - Part-time or full-time (based on performance and workload) - Long-term opportunity for the right person --- WORK SETUP REQUIREMENTS Please confirm the following when you apply: - Internet speed: Minimum 25 Mbps download / 10 Mbps upload (stable wired connection preferred) - Monitors: Dual monitors required — you will be working across Figma, Bricks Builder, and reference material simultaneously - Backup internet: Must have a backup connection (mobile hotspot or second ISP) for outages - Availability: 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM AWST, Monday to Friday. Must be available and responsive during these hours. - Power backup: UPS or alternative power solution for brownouts if applicable to your area - Workspace: Dedicated, quiet workspace free from distractions --- HOW TO APPLY To be considered, please send: 1. Tell us which pages are yours and what builder was used. 3. A short summary of your experience with Figma and Bricks Builder — how long you have used each, what types of sites you have built, and your typical workflow from design to live site. 4. Your current work setup — number of monitors, internet speed (screenshot of a speed test), backup internet, power backup 5. Your timezone and daily availability 6. Include the word BLUEPRINT in your application so we know you read this far Applications without real examples of both design and build work will not be considered. Screenshots of Figma designs with matching live site links are what we want to see. --- FINAL FILTER This role is for designer-builders who care about craft — not people who install a theme and move things around. job_title: Real Estate Video Editor — Luxury Properties | Final Cut Pro | Long-Term
description: Company: WorldClass Creative Location: Remote (Philippines preferred) Type: Full-time contractor Pay: Base + performance bonuses (details below) About This Role WorldClass Creative produces cinematic listing content for the $1M–$10M+ South Florida luxury real estate market. We work with high-end agents and developers in Palm Beach County, shooting properties that range from waterfront estates to new-construction residences. We're hiring editors for our post-production division. You will edit raw drone, interior, and exterior footage into polished listing reels and cinematic videos. You won't be shooting. You won't be managing clients. You'll edit, and you'll get good at our style fast. This is a long-term position. We're building a team, and the editors who prove themselves early will have first access to higher-tier projects and creative direction work as we grow. The Work: You'll produce two types of deliverables from raw 4K footage we provide: - Listing Reels (Vertical / 9:16) - 60–90 second social-format reels for Instagram. Shot selection, music, color grade, pacing. These are the bread and butter. - You'll edit 2–3 of these per day once you're ramped. - Cinematic Horizontal Videos (16:9) - 2–4 minute listing walkthroughs. Slower pace, more room to breathe. These take longer per piece but the footage is usually stronger. Typical daily output after your first two weeks: 2–3 completed videos. We provide the footage, music library, LUTs, and templates. You bring the edit instincts and the speed. Requirements: Final Cut Pro 11+ — this is non-negotiable. Our template library, LUT workflow, and project structure are built around FCP. If you edit in Premiere and want to switch, that's fine, but you need to be comfortable in FCP before your first project. 1–3 years editing real estate or architectural video. Wedding, travel, and corporate reels don't count. We need someone who already knows how luxury property footage should move, breathe, and cut. If your portfolio doesn't have at least 3 real estate edits, this isn't the right fit. Strong color grading instincts. You know the difference between warm-and-inviting interiors and orange-tinted mistakes. You can match shots across rooms without everything looking like the same filter. You grade for accuracy first, mood second. A computer that handles 4K without choking. No proxy-only workflows. You need to be able to scrub through 4K drone footage and interior clips without lag. If your machine can't do that, this role will frustrate you. Reliable internet and a quiet workspace. We communicate async through Frame.io and messaging. You need to upload finished exports (150–250MB files) without it taking all day. Available 9AM–1PM Eastern (US) for overlap. The rest of your hours are flexible. But during that 4-hour window, you respond to messages and feedback within 30 minutes. What You Don't Need: You don't need to talk to clients. David handles all client communication. You don't need to own a camera or any recording equipment. Compensation: Guaranteed base: $1,400 USD/month Volume bonuses (stack on top of base): Videos 9–20/month: +$25 per video Videos 21–35/month: +$30 per video Videos 36+/month: +$35 per video Quality bonus: $100–$200/month We score every edit on a 100-point quality scorecard. Average score of 85+ earns $100/month. Score of 92+ earns $200/month. What this looks like in practice: Learning - 20 videos/month (ramp period) ~$1,675 Consistent 85+ - 35 videos/month - ~$2,275 Scoring 90+ - 45 videos/month - ~ $2,950 Scoring 92+ - 55 videos/month - ~$3,550 Your earnings scale directly with your speed and quality. Editors who produce more and score higher make more. No cap on volume bonuses. Payment: bi-weekly via Gusto Our Standards: We edit luxury real estate. The audience is buyers considering a $3M home purchase. Every frame matters. How We Work: Frame.io for project delivery and review. You upload exports, David leaves timestamped feedback, you revise. Async communication. No daily standups. No Zoom calls unless something specific needs a screen share. You post a daily status update ("On track, delivering 3 edits by 9AM EST" or "Flagging an issue with the drone footage on Project X"). Short messages, clear information. Feedback loop. title: Direct Response Video Editor
description: If you understand what video hooks work, why pacing matters, and how editing decisions move performance metrics, this role was built for you. This is not an execution role. You won't be handed timestamps or told what footage to pull. You'll read a brief, make strong editorial calls, and ship high-performing paid social creatives at volume across Meta and TikTok. The creative strategists own the concept and messaging. You own the pacing, footage selection, hook strength, platform feel, and variations fast enough to fuel aggressive testing cycles. WHO THEY ARE You’ll be working with fast-growing DTC brands and performance creative teams scaling aggressively across Meta and TikTok. These brands operate in categories like wellness, beauty, supplements, fashion, personal care, and consumer products, all heavily focused on direct-response advertising, creative testing, and paid social scale. Most are spending aggressively on Meta and rely on fast iteration, high-volume testing, and performance-focused creative to drive growth. The teams operate with a lean, performance-driven culture where creativity is judged by results, not aesthetics. Editors are trusted to think independently, move quickly, collaborate closely with strategists and media buyers, and continuously improve output based on performance feedback. This is a fully remote, full-time role. WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU - Work with fast-growing DTC brands: Join ecommerce teams scaling aggressively through paid social advertising - Multiple immediate openings: Get matched with brands actively looking for editors right now - Creative ownership: Make real editorial decisions instead of acting as a production executor - Performance-focused environments: Work on ads designed specifically for testing, iteration, and measurable results - AI-driven workflows: Use modern AI tools for voiceovers, captioning, B-roll generation, and production acceleration - Growth opportunities: Potential to evolve into Senior Editor, Creative Strategist, or leadership roles as the brands continue scaling - Remote flexibility: Fully remote opportunities focused on output and execution rather than micromanagement WHAT YOU’RE GETTING INTO - Edit direct-response video ads for Meta, TikTok, and paid social placements using AI UGC, testimonials, product demos, B-roll, and creator footage - Apply direct-response editing principles, including hooks, pacing, retention management, CTA placement, and conversion-focused sequencing - Create multiple creative variations across hooks, pacing, visuals, CTAs, and angles to support testing cycles - Independently interpret creative briefs and select the strongest footage and visuals for each concept - Produce platform-native creative optimized for Reels, TikTok feeds, Shorts, and paid placements - Use AI-assisted workflows for voiceovers, captioning, B-roll generation, and creative optimization - Source music, overlays, stock footage, and supporting assets that improve engagement and conversion performance - Collaborate closely with Creative Strategists, media buyers, and founders to improve creative quality and performance outcomes - Deliver high-volume creative output while maintaining strong quality and fast turnaround times WHO YOU ARE - You have experience editing direct-response or paid social ads for Meta, TikTok, or YouTube Shorts for high-spend DTC ecommerce brands. - You understand direct-response editing deeply, including hooks, pacing, retention, engagement flow, and conversion-focused storytelling - You have experience with motion graphics, VSLs, or AI-generated creative workflows - You are familiar with performance metrics like hook rate, hold rate, thumbstop rate, CTR, and creative fatigue - You can independently turn a creative brief into a polished ad without needing every shot pre-selected - You have strong instincts for Reels/TikTok-native editing styles and modern paid social creative - You are proficient with Premiere Pro, After Effects, CapCut, Frame.io, Slack, and Google Drive - You are comfortable using AI-assisted editing workflows and emerging creative production tools - You can manage high creative output without sacrificing quality or attention to detail - You communicate clearly, take feedback professionally, and thrive in fast-moving remote environments - You are fluent in English WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE 30 Days: Understand the brand’s creative workflows, editing standards, and direct-response frameworks while producing video concepts independently. 60 Days: Consistently deliver high-performing concepts with strong pacing, hooks, creative variation, and efficient feedback implementation. 90 Days: Operate independently with a reliable production rhythm, contribute stronger creative ideas proactively, and consistently support performance goals through your editing decisions.

Our mission is to give people the freedom to work, explore, and stay connected anywhere. From Baja coastlines to deep forest trails, our customers rely on our gear for capability, protection, and unlimited connection. Your role is to help visually tell this story across all platforms. You must be highly experienced, creative, fast, and able to work autonomously within a growing brand. Responsibilities Video Editing – Long Form - Edit 6–15 minute YouTube videos with strong retention, pacing, and narrative clarity. - Add b-roll, overlays, captions, music, and brand-consistent graphics. - Build engaging openings with proven YouTube hook methods. Video Editing – Short Form - Execute the Hook ? Retain ? Reward method for Reels, TikTok, and Shorts. - Add dynamic subtitles, zooms, cuts, ---------- inserts, and pacing adjustments. - Produce scroll-stopping, high-retention content. Graphic Design & Photo Editing - Create YouTube thumbnails and graphic assets. - Design text treatments, overlays, and promotional visuals. - Edit lifestyle and product photos for multi-platform use. Brand Storytelling - Align all edits with our brand themes: freedom, connection, capability, control. - Contribute creative ideas and concepts for future video content. AI-Driven Editing & Workflow Optimization - Use AI tools (ChatGPT, Adobe AI, Topaz, Descript, etc.) as a core part of your editing workflow. - Generate high-performing hooks, captions, and on-screen text callouts using AI. - Use AI to research and improve storytelling, pacing, and content structure. - Continuously explore and implement new AI workflows to improve output quality, speed, and efficiency. - Leverage AI to enhance both creative output and production throughput, not just assist basic tasks. Cross-Platform Optimization - Edit in multiple aspect ratios: 16:9, 9:16, 4:5, 1:1. - Prepare final deliverables in organized, structured folders. - Optimize content for YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, Facebook . Collaboration - Work closely with the content team and leadership. - Follow SOPs and meet deadlines consistently. - Join scheduled calls proactively (no reminders required) - Be punctual and prepared for feedback sessions Work Discipline & Delivery Standards - Be actively available and responsive during working hours (PST schedule). - Address tasks, revisions, and team communication within working hours. - Meet deadlines consistently and communicate early if delays occur. - Submit deliverables early in the workday whenever possible to allow time for review and revisions. Quality & Output Standards - Deliver edits that are near publish-ready on first submission. - Ensure drafts require minimal revisions and are not incomplete or partially executed. - Perform a full self-review before submission to ensure: - all feedback is applied - no new issues are introduced - output meets brand and quality standards - Maintain consistently high production quality across all deliverables. Note: Include the phrase “Senior Video Editor Pro” in your subject line. Applications missing this phrase will not be considered. Use at least 5AP for your application. Required Skills - Ability to work graveyard shift (PST hours) - 3–5+ years professional video editing experience - Expert in Adobe Premiere Pro - Strong skills in After Effects, Photoshop, Illustrator, or Figma - Proven experience editing YouTube content and high-performing short-form videos - Strong understanding of retention, pacing, story structure, and attention engineering - Experience creating high-converting thumbnails - Strong understanding of modern content trends across YouTube, Instagram, and TikTok - Ability to edit lifestyle, outdoor, product, and UGC-style content AI & Workflow Skills (Required) - Strong proficiency in using AI tools (ChatGPT, Adobe AI, etc.) within editing workflows - Ability to generate hooks, captions, and on-screen text using AI - Experience using AI to improve storytelling, pacing, and video performance - Ability to research and implement new AI workflows to improve efficiency and output quality Work Ethic & Discipline - Highly reliable, responsive, and accountable - Strong attention to detail and ability to self-review work - Ability to follow feedback precisely and minimize repeated revisions Bonus Experience - Motion graphics or animation skills. - Experience in e-commerce, outdoor brands, or creator channels. - Understanding of YouTube SEO (titles, thumbnails, keywords). - Ability to generate ideas for hooks, storylines, and visual treatments. What We Offer - Long-term employment with growth potential. - Competitive salary based on experience. - Consistent weekly workload. - Direct impact on a fast-scaling global brand. - Creative freedom and an opportunity to lead our video direction. How to Apply Submit the following: - Resume - Short explanation of why you’re the right fit - Brief explanation of how you use AI in your editing workflow - 1 example where you improved video performance (retention, CTR, etc.) - Portfolio of your best long-form and short-form edits - Links to YouTube channels or brands you’ve edited for Learn About Us: ---------- ---------- ---------- Website: ----------

title: Creative Director
description: The Vision — Read This First I am going to be honest with you because I believe the right person for this role needs to understand what they are stepping into. I am building more than a YouTube channel. I am documenting a life mission — from the very beginning, raw and unfiltered. I am at the start of my e-commerce journey right now. Not at the top looking back. Not telling you a success story. I am at day one, and that is exactly the point. My life purpose, the thing I believe God put me on this earth to do, is to build an e-commerce company that I will grow and eventually exit for at least $500 million — and use that money to fund a charity that does real, lasting good for people and for this planet. That is not a fantasy. That is the plan. And I am going to document every single step — from the very first sale to the final exit. The wins, the failures, the sleepless nights, the breakthroughs, the lessons — all of it, completely raw and unfiltered. No highlight reel. No pretending to have it figured out. Just the real journey as it happens, so that others can learn from it, be inspired by it, and maybe find their own purpose along the way. This content will run for the next 20 to 30 years. You are not joining a finished product — you are joining at the ground floor of something that will grow into something massive. And I need someone by my side who does not just edit videos but who truly believes in this mission and wants to help bring it to life. I am not looking for a freelancer who edits a few clips and moves on. I am looking for a creative partner — someone who will grow with me from the very beginning, who will help shape how the world sees this journey, and who will one day look back and say: "I was there from day one. description: Remote · Full-time · $1.5K–4K/mo + uncapped performance bonuses Hey, I'm Yente, co-founder of Primal Storm. In 9 months, we went from a $1,000 CPA and zero customers to $1M+/month in revenue. Now we're scaling to $5M/month by December. We're hiring 2 editors to help us get there. Why we exist: Men are getting weaker every day. Destroyed by modern society. Softer, slower, smaller versions of who they were built to be. Our mission is to restore the balance. To empower men toward a healthy lifestyle through natural products and real community. To make them thrive again. Men are warriors, not victims. That's not a slogan. That's the standard. Every ad you ship serves that mission. Every winner you build helps another man take his power back. What you'll actually do: - Edit 7–10 ads per week that go straight into real spend. - Work with UGC, AI clips, and the best raw footage in the men's supplement space. - See your creatives scale to $10K+/day, or fail fast and learn faster. - Build toward becoming a creative strategist (this is the path, not the ceiling). Required: Import episodes from podcast host RSS feed Auto-create episode pages from imported episodes Pull in title, date, description, audio/player, and episode artwork where available Support automatic or scheduled publishing Allow manual transcript entry after import Make season/topic tagging fast and simple in the admin panel Episode Pages Each episode page should include: Episode title Short hook Embedded audio player Subscribe/listen buttons Key takeaways Practice / experiment Transcript section Related episodes by topic Newsletter signup CTA Episodes Index The Episodes page should include: Search bar Season filter Topic filter Format filter Episode cards with title, hook, play button, transcript/show notes link, and tags Newsletter Integration The site must include newsletter signup for Starter Week. Preferred Skills and Experience Strong WordPress design and development experience Experience building podcast, media, creator, education, or speaker websites Experience with podcast RSS feed imports Experience creating custom post types, taxonomies, and custom fields Strong responsive design skills Strong UI/UX sense SEO setup experience GA4 and Search Console setup experience Experience with newsletter integrations Ability to build clean admin workflows Good communication and reliable project management Ability to explain technical decisions clearly Preferred Tools / Platforms Experience with any of the following is helpful: WordPress Gutenberg/block editor Advanced Custom Fields Custom Post Type UI or custom-coded CPTs Elementor, only if lightweight and not overused Rank Math or Yoast WP Rocket, W3 Total Cache, or similar caching tools Gravity Forms, Fluent Forms, Contact Form 7, or similar beehiiv Substack ConvertKit MailerLite Mailchimp Google Analytics 4 Google Search Console Figma Adobe XD Canva Important Notes Please do not apply if you only build simple landing pages from generic templates. title: Part-Time YouTube Editor
description: Part-Time YouTube Editor for a Leadership & Authority Brand Talking-head content experience required. If your portfolio is travel, gaming, or short-form only, this role is not a fit. Part-time · Remote | $400–$650/month | Full-time path available | Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve Hi there! I'm a keynote speaker and executive coach advising C-suite executives at companies like L'Oréal, Mercedes-Benz, and Accenture on leadership and authority-building in the AI era. My YouTube channel is the next chapter of that work to reach the executives, consultants, and coaches. Not a side experiment. Not a "let's try YouTube for 3 months." A serious build with a serious audience in mind. For this I need a committed video editor. Is this you? This collaboration starts part-time, but full-time is on the table. As the channel grows, so does the workload — and I'd rather promote someone who already knows the brand than hire a stranger. If you're excellent and committed, the path to a full-time role (and full-time pay) is real and explicitly planned for. If you've been burned before, here's what's different Most editors who apply to posts like this have the same story: a client who started strong, gave vague feedback, disappeared for weeks, then ended it with no warning. Or a creator who promised "long-term" and churned through three editors in a year because they never built a real workflow. I've built and run programs for C-suite executives. I know what structured feedback looks like. You'll get a detailed style guide before your first edit, written notes on every revision round, and a predictable content calendar so you can plan your week. The goal is not to find someone to fill a slot. It's to find someone worth promoting. If you're excellent, diligent, and done being treated like a vendor — this is the role. What you'll edit - Talking-head videos (10–15 min) with B-roll, lower thirds, and motion graphics — context cards on a black background are a core part of the visual style - Clean audio treatment: noise reduction, leveling, breath cuts - Color grading to match a consistent, refined look - Captions formatted to brand style: clean, minimal, sentence case - Short-form clips (60 sec) cut from the same raw footage for LinkedIn and Instagram What I'm looking for - Talking-head experience: your portfolio must include at least 2 full YouTube videos (10+ min) of talking-head or interview-style content edited for another creator. Self-edited content, travel videos, and gaming content do not qualify. - Motion graphics: you know how to use simple text-based context cards to anchor the viewer — not heavy animation, just clean and purposeful - Tool proficiency: Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve — tell me your version - Reliable internet: minimum 10 Mbps upload. Power backup for outages is a strong plus - Overlap hours: at least 2–3 hours between 9am–6pm CET daily - Strong communicator: clear English, complete sentences, proactive updates. How you write to me during the hiring process tells me how you'll work with me long-term. - Growth-minded: you want to build something, not fill a slot Not a fit if: your only long-form examples are self-edited or travel/lifestyle videos, you're currently upskilling toward talking-head editing, or you expect above $700/month for a part-time start. The hiring process 01 — You apply via the screening form below. Takes 10–15 minutes. No CV needed. 02 — Portfolio review — I look specifically at pacing on talking-head content, motion graphics quality, and audio treatment 03 — Paid test edit — 3–5 shortlisted candidates receive a raw clip with a brief and style reference. You'll be paid $25–$40. Deadline: 48 hours. 04 — Async Loom interview — 3–5 min video walking through your edit. No live call required. 05 — 30-day paid trial — structured month with clear deliverables, a style guide, and detailed feedback on every edit The trial month & path forward Month 1 — Paid trial $300–$350 flat. Deliverable: 4 videos to completion, max 2 revision rounds each. You receive a full style guide, reference videos, and written feedback on every edit. Months 2–3 — Active part-time contract $400–$550/month. 4–6 videos/month, 3–4 day turnaround from raw delivery. Predictable schedule, content calendar, clear revision policy. Month 4+ — Established rate & full-time opportunity Strong performers move to $600–$650/month part-time. As the channel grows, the right person moves into a full-time role with expanded scope and expanded pay. I don't churn editors. I grow with them. Timeline Days 1–3: Applications open Day 4: Portfolio review Days 5–7: Paid test edits Days 8–9: Loom interviews Day 10: Trial contract signed Week 2–3: First full video delivered How to apply — read this carefully Start your application with the subject line or first line: LONG-FORM. Applications without this word will not be reviewed. Then complete the screening form below. It covers your portfolio, tools, availability, and your approach to motion graphics in talking-head content. Clear, complete answers are part of the evaluation, thin or vague responses are disqualifying. Only applicants who complete the form will be considered. Form link: ----------

title: Video Editor (DTC eCommerce)
description: About Us We are a fast-growing health and wellness brand obsessed with customer psychology and creative excellence. We don't just "make content," we build high-performance assets that drive millions in revenue. We are looking for a Video Editor who is genuinely passionate about performance, speed, and continuous improvement. This is not a role for someone who just wants to follow a storyboard and clock out. We need a creative who looks at a hook and immediately thinks of three ways to make it more engaging, faster, and higher-converting. Our philosophy: we prioritize 10 ads at 80% quality over 2 ads at 100%. Speed and volume win in performance marketing. If you're someone who obsesses over pixel-perfect polish at the expense of output, this isn't the right fit. The Role You will own the creation of high-volume, high-performance video ads, targeting 10–20 videos per week depending on length. This includes short-form for Meta/TikTok, long-form VSLs, AI avatars, B-roll edits, and voiceover-driven content. You'll work from creative briefs and scripts provided by our creative strategists and copywriters, turning direction into polished, high-converting assets at speed. You take deep pride in ownership, turn raw footage and AI outputs into systematic creative machines, and ensure our creative output is a competitive advantage. If you are a builder who thrives on iterating based on data rather than just "vibes," we want to talk to you. What You Will Do * Full-Spectrum Production: Create high-converting short-form ads (15–60s), UGC-style content, and long-form VSLs for Meta, TikTok, and YouTube. * AI Mastery: Take full ownership of our AI tech stack, including Veo 3, HeyGen, Runway, and ElevenLabs for video, and Nano-Banana for statics, to produce high-quality AI video, avatar, and voiceover outputs at scale. * Source Fresh Creatives: Proactively find and source fresh B-roll and visual assets from across the internet. You never run dry, and you never recycle. What We're Looking For Experience & Skills * 2+ years of video editing experience, with specific experience editing for DTC brands or performance marketing. * Technical mastery: Fluency in Premiere, Final Cut, or CapCut, plus advanced proficiency in AI video tools (Veo 3, HeyGen, Runway, ElevenLabs, Nano-Banana). * Strategic thinking: Strong instincts for hooks, pacing, and storytelling in a Direct Response (DR) context. * Resourcefulness: Proven ability to source fresh creatives, B-roll, and visual assets independently. You always have new material to work with. Work Style * Speed over perfection. You can move fast and deliver high volume without sacrificing the quality that matters. * Implement feedback quickly, often same-day turnaround. * Improvement-driven: You can demonstrate how you've personally improved a creative's performance through iteration or better editing workflows. * Excellent English, clear written and verbal communication for seamless collaboration. * Self-learner. You figure things out on your own. Whether it's a new tool, a new technique, or a new platform, you don't wait to be taught. * Organized file structures and version control for rapid iteration. Commitment Full-time and exclusive. This role requires your full professional focus. We invest heavily in our people, training, tools, growth, and we're looking for someone who's equally invested in building something long-term with us. Click here to apply : ----------
